summary.title: Formalizing Latent Thoughts: Four Axioms of Thought Representation in LLMs

setting_and_object.category: Evaluation protocol (axiomatic framework with intrinsic metrics)

details: Continuous/latent "thought representations" in LLMs are judged almost exclusively by downstream task accuracy, which conflates representation quality with model capacity and prevents attributing failures to the representation itself
No principled definition exists of what a latent thought representation must functionally do

An axiomatic characterization of a thought representation T as a latent functional state mediating input to semantic output, defined by four functional axioms: Causality (T can substitute the reasoning prefix's effect on the answer distribution), Minimality (information-bottleneck-style compression of input while retaining output relevance), Separability (a bounded-capacity projection can resolve semantically distinct outputs), Stability (T encodes the output distribution, incl. mode-collapse resistance and lexical invariance)

One computable measure per axiom, evaluated directly on the frozen source LLM without retraining and decoupled from downstream accuracy: KL substitution error, a cross-entropy surrogate IB gap Delta_IB = CE(X|Y,T) - CE(Y|T), same-/cross-task discriminator accuracy, and a Distributional Consistency Score (AUROC of a probe predicting non-zero semantic entropy)
Accompanying theoretical claims that the four axioms are consistent, mutually independent (via four counter-models each violating one axiom), and complete
Last Input Token (LIT) hidden states: all-layers variant and final-layer variant
Soft Thinking without noise (ST) and with Gumbel noise (STN), and Latent Thinking (LT), each at 1, 16, 32, 64, 128 thinking steps

Reference anchors: Output Embedding (Exact and Pooled) as an upper bound, Input Embedding (IE) of the prompt as the "adds nothing beyond the prompt" reference, and a Random Vector as information-free baseline

Five open-weight LLMs spanning dense, sparse-MoE, reasoning-distilled and RL-trained paradigms: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Skywork-OR1-32B, GPT-OSS-20B
All 23 tasks of Big Bench Extra Hard (BBEH) with the original benchmark prompts
Beam search returning 8 distinct sequences (up to 8192 tokens) per prompt to approximate the high-probability region of P(Y|x)
Probes: frozen Llama-3.2-1B backbone with a trainable projection into its token-embedding space plus a trained classification head; Causality projection trained on the source model's own outputs
Semantic equivalence classes for semantic entropy computed via thresholded cosine similarity of Embed-Nemotron-8B output embeddings
Bootstrap-paired gaps to the Input Embedding reference reported as |z|-scores
Sensitivity of Causality to answer-window length and number of substituted positions; minimal-projection control
Sensitivity of DCS to the similarity threshold tau; per-step DCS trajectories
Probe-capacity ablation and geometric analysis of within-task effective dimensionality; per-task correlation of Separability with downstream BBEH accuracy

key_findings.finding: Candidate thought representations retain coarse task identity but collapse on per-question identity within a task.
key_findings.evidence: Cross-task discriminator accuracy is near saturation for every candidate including the Input Embedding reference, while same-task accuracy is near the random baseline for all candidates except the Output Embedding anchor (whose best same-task accuracy is only 73%); a geometric analysis attributes this to too few effective within-task dimensions rather than probe capacity.

key_findings.finding: No audited candidate encodes information beyond the input prompt embedding: none consistently exceeds the Input Embedding reference on any axis.
key_findings.evidence: Averaged across LLMs, no candidate beats IE on Causality, Minimality, Separability, or Stability; per-LLM advantages do not generalize across models; IE even scores highest on Stability for Llama-3.3-70B, indicating distributional uncertainty is predictable from question text alone.

key_findings.finding: Intrinsic representational failures are invisible to downstream benchmark accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: Models can score well on BBEH while their representations fail to distinguish two questions from the same task; the per-task correlation between Separability and downstream accuracy shows the collapse is not explained by task difficulty.

key_findings.finding: Iterative latent-thinking representations degrade as the number of thinking steps increases.
key_findings.evidence: DCS (Stability AUROC) decreases with growing step count for both soft-thinking and latent-thinking families across 1/16/32/64/128 steps, with the largest degradation for Latent Thinking; Soft Thinking with Gumbel noise is the main Stability outlier below the IE reference.

key_findings.finding: The failure pattern is structural rather than a function of scale or training procedure, and differs by axis in an interpretable way.
key_findings.evidence: The same collapse appears across dense, sparse-MoE, reasoning-distilled, and RL-trained models from 8B to 70B; on Minimality, iterative thinking families sit at or above IE while Last Input Token falls below it, consistent with LIT retaining input-specific detail not used in the output.
